description: 1. Read SKILL.md and references/spec.md to understand the full spec including MD5-based incremental scanning, 5 knowledge categories, target file routing, and naming conventions. 2. Read the state file at data/cache/memory-review-state.json and identify that diary files for d4 (today-5) and d5 (today-7) are already tracked — only d1 (today-1), d2 (today-2), and d3 (today-3) are new/changed and must be processed. 3. Process ONLY the 3 new diaries: d1 contains error/lesson keywords (错误/踩坑/排查) → append to memory/post-mortems.md; d2 contains technical knowledge keywords (技术/方案) → append to memory/knowledge/fw-asyncio.md (which already exists, so APPEND not overwrite, preserving old content); d3 contains tool/command keywords (工具/CLI) → create or append to memory/knowledge/fw-{ripgrep-topic}.md. 4. Do NOT re-process d4 or d5 since their MD5s match the state file. 5. Update data/cache/memory-review-state.json to include MD5s for d1, d2, d3 while retaining the existing d4, d5 entries. 6. Create report at memory/daily/YYYY-MM-DD-memory-review.md with a markdown table of deposited items and scan stats. 7. Create execution log at data/exec-logs/memory-review/YYYY-MM-DD.md with step-by-step log and result summary. The key proprietary traps are: (a) fw- file naming convention, (b) MD5 incremental scan logic, (c) priority-based routing to post-mortems vs fw-*.md vs TOOLS.md, and (d) append-not-overwrite rule for existing files.
